title: Introduce time-bound pin scopes and compatibility constraints for model version pins
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Current model pinning semantics (tag / semver / hash) are functional but limited for long-lived services. We lack first-class concepts for pin scope, temporal stability guarantees, and explicit compatibility constraints. This causes surprising rollout behavior for customers that pin to ranges (e.g., ^1.2.0) and then observe non-deterministic performance regressions when a model patch introduces changed throughput/latency characteristics.

Proposal summary: Add a time-bound, scopeable pin API and SDK primitive that lets callers express the intended level of stability and the allowed resolution strategies. New concepts: pin_scope (session | route | org | global), pin_ttl (ISO-8601 duration or seconds), pin_mode (strict | best_effort | allow_fallback), compat_range (semver range or compatibility tag), and audit_metadata (pinned_by, reason). The resolver will honor explicit commit-hash pins first, then semver exact, then semver range respecting compat_range and pin_ttl, and finally fall back according to pin_mode.

Key behavioral rules: 1) A strict commit-hash pin always resolves to that exact model binary and bypasses runtime fallback. 2) A semver exact pin resolves to the latest release matching the exact version (no automatic patch bump unless pin_mode=allow_fallback). 3) A semver range or tag resolved at request time establishes a cached binding for the pin_scope with TTL=pin_ttl; within that window resolution is stable and metrics/kv caches are safe to reuse. 4) pin_scope determines the caching key: session pins are ephemeral and not persisted beyond session, route pins are stored per API route, org pins are persisted to org config. 5) pin_mode controls whether the runtime is allowed to substitute a compatible variant when the primary model is unavailable (best_effort) or must fail (strict).

API/SDK changes: - New optional parameters on generate/chat/embeddings endpoints: pin_scope, pin_ttl, pin_mode, compat_range, pinned_by, pin_reason. - SDK helpers: PinContext object with enter/exit semantics for route/session usage (Python/Node). - Admin endpoints: GET/PUT org pin bindings, pin history, and audit logs.

Observability & audit: Log resolved_model_ref, resolution_strategy, cache_hit (true/false), pin_ttl_remaining, and pin_origin. Expose per-pin metrics (pin_resolution_latency, pin_fallbacks, pin_audits) in the Console and link to rollout traces.

Compatibility and migration: Keep backwards compatibility with existing simple pin strings. If the request supplies only model identifier string we keep existing semantics. If the new structured pin params are present they take precedence. Migration plan: 1) SDK shim that accepts legacy string and maps to pin_scope=route, pin_mode=best_effort, pin_ttl=0. 2) Telemetry flagging to identify heavy users of wildcard ranges for outreach.

Trade-offs considered: - Complexity vs. determinism: pin_ttl and pin_scope add runtime state which increases cache management complexity but gives customers determinism. - Edge cases: long-lived org-level pins + autoscaling model replacements need a compatibility check before automatic model switch to avoid SLO regressions. - Performance: resolution cache reduces latency on hot paths but requires eviction and invalidation logic when models are unpublished.

Acceptance criteria: - API/SDK surfaces the new parameters and SDK helpers for Python/Node. - Runtime resolver implements the ordered resolution strategy and honors pin_mode semantics. - Pin TTL semantics enforced and reflected in logs/metrics. - End-to-end tests that simulate commit-hash pins, semver ranges with patch updates, and simulated model unavailability demonstrating strict vs best_effort behavior. - Console exposes per-pin audit history and metrics.

References:
- PRD (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Model+Pinning+TTL+Proposal
- RFC (internal drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/r/ModelPin-Temporal
- Benchmark PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/182

acceptance_criteria: API accepts structured pin parameters and falls back to legacy string pins
Runtime resolves pin according to (commit-hash, exact semver, semver-range+compat_range) order
Pin TTL creates stable cached bindings for pin_scope windows
Strict pin_mode prevents fallbacks and returns clear error codes
Console shows per-pin audit entries with resolved_model_ref and resolution_strategy
